source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: P.J. Washington
injuries.short_comment: Washington (illness/shoulder) is listed as out for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
injuries.long_comment: Washington was initially listed on the injury report due to a shoulder issue. Since then, he developed an illness and was downgraded to doubtful. Washington will now miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign, with his next opportunity to play coming Sunday in Utah. In the meantime, Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher are candidates for more minutes.

injuries.name: Dereck Lively II
injuries.short_comment: Head coach Dusty May said Friday that Lively (foot) is moving well and progressing in his recovery, and the big man told May he's "close" to returning, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
injuries.long_comment: Lively hasn't seen game action since Nov. 21, 2025, and he remains without a firm timetable to return after undergoing right foot surgery last December. However, this update suggests that the big man is trending in the right direction.

injuries.name: Tobi Lawal
injuries.short_comment: Lawal (groin) is out for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
injuries.long_comment: Lawal will miss a second straight game with right groin tightness. The rookie forward isn't expected to have a big role in the rotation, so he likely won't have much fantasy upside anytime soon. His next chance to play will come Sunday against the Jazz on the second leg of a back-to-back set.

injuries.name: Tarik Biberovic
injuries.short_comment: Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injuries.long_comment: Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injuries.name: Sergio de Larrea
injuries.short_comment: De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injuries.long_comment: De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

injuries.name: Jusuf Nurkic
injuries.short_comment: Nurkic (foot) has been cleared for on-court work and will be re-evaluated in one week.
injuries.long_comment: Nurkic continues to make progress in his recovery from a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe on his right foot, and getting cleared for on-court work is a big step in his rehab. There are still a few steps he'll need to clear before he makes his return to the floor, but once he's able to get through full-contact, 5-on-5 work, we'll know he's close.

injuries.name: Lauri Markkanen
injuries.short_comment: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long_comment: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

injuries.name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
injuries.short_comment: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.long_comment: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.
